description: We are Université de Montréal students in computer science and machine learning.
summary:
Taupin is a web app that helps a farmer compare crop rotations for one field. The farmer enters the field's location and ticks what matters on the farm: water in dry years, soil loss, nitrogen to buy, crop residue, or pests. The app pulls 25 years of daily rain from NASA GPM IMERG, air temperature and root-zone soil wetness from NASA POWER, and soil moisture from NASA SMAP. It then ranks four five-year rotations, including the current one, and shows for each why it ranks there, the evidence, the benefits against the current rotation, the information gaps and the risks.

The field is drawn in 3D from 1 m lidar, satellite vegetation and soil maps, with zones that show where to scout. A photo model that runs on the phone names soil animals such as wireworms (92.5 % on 756 test photos) and pins each photo on the field.

Rain now swings widely from year to year, and a rotation is a five-year commitment. Taupin puts the evidence in front of the farmer, who makes the decision.
details:
Taupin is an open source project that helps a farmers compare crop rotations for one field. The farmer taps the field on a map and ticks what matters on the farm: water in dry years, soil loss, nitrogen to buy, crop residue, or pests. The app pulls 25 years of daily rain from NASA GPM IMERG, air temperature, soil temperature and root-zone soil wetness from NASA POWER, and soil moisture from NASA SMAP. It then ranks seven five-year rotations, including the current one, and shows for each why it ranks there, the evidence, the benefits against the current rotation, the information gaps and the risks.

The field is built in 3D in the browser from elevation data (national lidar where it exists, global terrain tiles elsewhere), NASA HLS plant cover and SoilGrids soil data, with zones that show where to scout. Our example field is in Quebec, where Canadian lidar and crop maps add detail. A photo model that runs on the phone names soil animals such as wireworms (92.5 % on 756 test photos) and pins each photo on the field. Unclear photos go to the lab.

Rain now swings widely from year to year, and a rotation is a five-year commitment. Taupin puts the evidence in front of the farmer, who makes the decision. Built with Python, JavaScript, Three.js, ONNX Runtime Web and DINOv2. It runs offline, and the code and model are open.
